newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end higher on interest rate hopes.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end higher on interest rate hopes.

text.p: Italian stocks ended higher on Tuesday after a firmer start on Wall Street and encouraging data on Italy inflation for April, while domestic bonds were also higher, dealers said.
April's CPI inflation came in as expected at 1.7 percent year-on-year from March's 2.2 percent leading to some hopes of a cut in interest rates soon, they added.
Agnelli family holding IFIL ended higher after news it was to form a new retail grouping with French Auchan which would include its controlled stake in Rinascente.
All-share Mibtel index ended up 0.74 percent at 12,424 and the Mib30 blue chip index 0.83 percent firmer at 18,546.
IFIL ended up 4.32 percent at 5,173 lire while Rinascente was suspended for the day pending the announcement with Auchan and its capital increase for 780 billion lire.

After the failed textile merger at the weekend, shares in Mediobanca and HPI recovered, while Marzotto forged ahead. HPI ended up 1.15 percent at 873.3 lire, Mediobanca was 2.07 percent firmer at 10,376 and Marzotto 3.17 percent higher at 12,811.

Fiat shares ended up 1.81 percent at 5,798 lire after Roberto Testore, the managing director of Fiat Auto, said on Monday the Italian car market had grown by more than 40 percent in April compared with the same month last year.
Official data is due to be published by the Transport Ministry on Friday May 9 or Saturday May 10.

ENI shares up after it agreed on Monday to set up a new electricity production group with ENEL. ENI up 0.8 percent at 8,717 lire but private electricity production group Edison closed off 3.65 percent at 8,711 lire on fear of tougher competition from the new grouping.
